headline: Apollo’s Slok says AI has delivered zero financial payoff outside tech
body: Apollo’s Torsten Slok says AI has delivered “zero financial payoff” to corporate America outside of tech. In a note on what he calls the S&P 493, profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat.
note: The claim covers the S&P 500 minus seven large tech stocks, a wider group than tech alone.
correction: The note said the claim says little about AI spending inside banks and asset managers. The source does not say that, and the S&P 493 is the S&P 500 minus seven tech names, so the note now states only that definition.

evidence.text: AI hasn’t benefited the bottom line of any big corporations outside the tech industry, according to a note recently published by the chief economist at Apollo Global Management (the private equity giant that used to own TechCrunch).

Apollo’s Torsten Slok focuses on what he calls the S&P 493 — the S&P 500, minus Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Tesla — finding that profit margins and revenue per worker appear to be flat, with no evidence that AI is improving productivity.
“Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech,” Slok said.
